dedupe_keys.name: yaounde cameroon gis network analysis to optimise e waste collection points and routes

description: This case study plans how to expand formal collection of electronic waste in Yaoundé, the capital of Cameroon, where most e-waste moves through informal channels. Yannick Esopere and Helmut Yabar of the University of Tsukuba posted it as a preprint on Preprints.org in February 2026. The current system has three streams, informal, formal and municipal solid waste collection, with only three formal collection points. Using a survey and GIS network analysis, the authors allocated eight more collection points to maximise formal coverage and compared three collection routes for fuel cost and greenhouse gas emissions. The preprint is available online, free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Coverage is the city. Caveats: it is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, and the survey data are not published. Formal collection coverage rose by 52.81 percent in the maximised scenario; route 1 was the cheapest, at about 2.07 million CFA francs a year in fuel, and the lowest emitter, at about 6,715 kg CO2 equivalent a year; moving to an integrated e-waste system cut emissions by 13.83 percent, equal to 3.04 percent of Cameroon's 2030 target under its nationally determined contribution. Simulation uses: collection point siting and route cost figures for e-waste reverse logistics models in African cities. Related records: the Global E-waste Monitor (data-global-e-waste-monitor) gives national e-waste generation.
